newsitem.title: USA: US May budget gap $48.49 bln, down from year ago.
newsitem.headline: US May budget gap $48.49 bln, down from year ago.

text.p: The government posted a budget deficit of $48.49 billion in May, the Treasury Department said on Friday, down 8.6 percent from the $53.05 billion deficit posted a year earlier in May 1996.
Last month's deficit followed a $93.94 billion surplus in April, when revenues were boosted by payments from individuals complying with the mid-month filing deadline for 1996 tax returns.
Total outlays in May were $142.99 billion, up from $134.65 billion in April but down from $143.17 billion spent in May 1996.
Revenues from taxes, fees and other sources dropped to $94.49 billion in May from $228.59 billion in April. A year earlier in May 1996, the government took in $90.12 billion of revenues.

During the first eight months of fiscal 1997 that ends on Sept 30, the cumulative budget deficit dropped 40 percent to $65.39 billion from $108.36 billion in the comparable first eight months of fiscal 1996.

The improvement in the deficit for May and for the first eight months of the year would have been even greater except that military active pay, veterans' benefits and supplemental security income payments scheduled for June 1 were moved up to May 30.
The payments were made early because June 1 fell on a weekend and waiting till after that time to mail out government checks would have meant delays for recipients.
During May, receipts from individual tax payments dropped back to $30.7 billion from $134.3 billion in April. Corporate tax payments declined to $4.3 billion in May from $27.4 billion in April.
The Clinton administration has officially forecast a deficit for all of fiscal 1997 of $125.59 billion, compared with a $107.4 billion shortfall in fiscal 1996.

But a steadily expanding economy that has swelled the government's tax receipts appears certain to bring the deficit well under the official estimate, which is expected to be revised when the White House issues its midyear economic review later this year.

Private-sector analysts say the fiscal 1997 deficit will more likely be the range of $70 billion to $100 billion, which would mark a fifth straight year of improvement since the government's spending deficit peaked at $290.4 billion in fiscal 1992.
